page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.16xlarge is a Nitro-based, general-purpose server instance configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores and 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. Powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor, the platform includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and VNNI. The system bundles 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput in memory-intensive and vectorized workloads. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 218.61 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 95.85 GB/sec, placing memory transfer capabilities in the top tier. The instance also delivers strong vector execution in PassMark extended instructions tests with a score of 55665.26. However, single-threaded processing reflects architectural tradeoffs, with single-core stress-ng, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression scores placing in the lower quartile.

Multi-core execution remains balanced across general compute routines, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 12132.0, PassMark CPU score of 44173.28, and Redis throughput of 52.21 million SET operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 36.86 GB/sec. Large language model inference tasks show moderate prompt ingestion speed but limited token generation throughput due to the lack of dedicated acceleration hardware.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 75 Gbps networking baseline, and fast local NVMe storage, the m5dn.16xlarge is suited for transactional databases, distributed caching nodes, multi-threaded batch data transformations, and containerized enterprise application backends requiring high transient disk IOPS.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 64 vCPUs and 32 dedicated physical cores on a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. It provides 256 GB of DDR4 memory, 2400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and a 75 Gbps baseline network capacity on the AWS Nitro system. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 218 GB/sec read and strong AVX-512 vector instruction execution, though single-core throughput ranks in lower brackets. The platform achieves solid multi-core processing performance, managing 52.21 million Redis operations per second and 36.86 GB/sec static web throughput. Without dedicated GPUs, text generation benchmarks remain modest. The system serves as an efficient balance for enterprise databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput data processing workflows requiring fast local scratch storage.
